style="vertical-align:bottom;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"><div style="overflow:hidden;height:20px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="vertical-align:bottom;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"><div style="overflow:hidden;height:20px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="vertical-align:bottom;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"><div style="overflow:hidden;height:20px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div></td></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:bottom;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"><div style="text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><a style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;" href="#s1E74A09EE12B5BE8BFBC037CA7B8E5F9"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Signatures</font></a></div></td><td style="vertical-align:bottom;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"><div style="overflow:hidden;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div></td><td style="vertical-align:bottom;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"><div style="text-align:right;font-size:9pt;"><a style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;" href="#s1E74A09EE12B5BE8BFBC037CA7B8E5F9">69</a></div></td></tr></table></div></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div><br></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><a name="s5527F40A255654E5BF30A2CF96680752"></a></div><div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;font-size:7pt;"><a style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;" href="#s2AB1C425F68D5726B01A88D75B434628"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;">Table of Contents</font></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:7pt;"><a style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;" href="#s26AA4B5CED4051F38E975FF750EB2944"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;">Index to Financial Statements</font></a></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:center;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">GLOSSARY OF OIL AND NATURAL GAS TERMS</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The following are abbreviations and definitions of certain terms used in this document, which are commonly used in the oil and natural gas industry:</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">3-D seismic</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Geophysical data that depict the subsurface strata in three dimensions. 3-D seismic typically provides a more detailed and accurate interpretation of the subsurface strata than 2-D, or two-dimensional, seismic.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Analogous</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">reservoir</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Analogous reservoirs, as used in resources assessments, have similar rock and fluid properties, reservoir conditions (depth, temperature and pressure) and drive mechanisms, but are typically at a more advanced stage of development than the reservoir of interest and thus may provide concepts to assist in the interpretation of more limited data and estimation of recovery. When used to support proved reserves, an analogous reservoir refers to a reservoir that shares the following characteristics with the reservoir of interest: (i)&#160;same geological formation (but not necessarily in pressure communication with the reservoir of interest); (ii)&#160;same environment of deposition; (iii)&#160;similar geological structure; and (iv)&#160;same drive mechanism. For a complete definition of analogous reservoir, refer to the SEC&#8217;s Regulation&#160;S-X, Rule&#160;4-10(a)(2).</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Basin</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;A large natural depression on the earth&#8217;s surface in which sediments have accumulated.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Bbl</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;One stock tank barrel, or 42 U.S. gallons liquid volume, used herein in reference to crude oil, condensate, NGLs or water.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Boe</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;One barrel of oil equivalent, calculated by converting natural gas to oil equivalent barrels at a ratio of six Mcf of natural gas to one Bbl of oil. This is an energy content correlation and does not reflect a value or price relationship between the commodities.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Boe/d</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;One Boe per day.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">British thermal unit or Btu</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of a one-pound mass of water from 58.5 to 59.5 degrees Fahrenheit.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Completion</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The installation of permanent equipment for production of oil, natural gas or NGLs or, in the case of a dry well, reporting to the appropriate authority that the well has been abandoned.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Condensate</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;A mixture of hydrocarbons that exists in the gaseous phase at original reservoir temperature and pressure, but that, when produced, is in the liquid phase at surface pressure and temperature.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Developed</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">acreage</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The number of acres that are allocated or assignable to productive wells or wells capable of production.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Development</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">costs</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Costs incurred to obtain access to proved reserves and to provide facilities for extracting, treating, gathering and storing the oil and natural gas. For a complete definition of development costs, refer to the SEC&#8217;s Regulation&#160;S-X, Rule&#160;4-10(a)(7).</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Development</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">project</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The means by which petroleum resources are brought to the status of economically producible. As examples, the development of a single reservoir or field, an incremental development in a producing field or the integrated development of a group of several fields and associated facilities may constitute a development project.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Development</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">well</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;A well drilled within the proved area of an oil or natural gas reservoir to the depth of a stratigraphic horizon known to be productive.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Differential</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;An adjustment to the price of oil or natural gas from an established spot market price to reflect differences in the quality and/or location of oil or natural gas.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Dry</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">well</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;A well found to be incapable of producing hydrocarbons in commercial quantities such that proceeds from the sale of such production do not exceed production expenses and taxes.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Economically producible</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The term economically producible, as it relates to a resource, means a resource which generates revenue that exceeds, or is reasonably expected to exceed, the costs of the operation. For a complete definition of economically producible, refer to the SEC&#8217;s Regulation&#160;S-X, Rule&#160;4-10(a)(10).</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Estimated ultimate recovery or EUR</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The sum of estimated reserves remaining as of a given date and cumulative production as of that date.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Ethane rejection.</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;&#32;&#32;&#32;&#32;Ethane rejection occurs when ethane is left in the wellhead gas stream when the gas is processed, rather than being extracted and sold as a liquid after fractionation.&#160; When ethane is left in the gas stream, the Btu content of the residue gas sold is higher and marginally increases the realized price of residue gas; conversely, the volumes of NGLs sold are lower and the average realized price for NGLs sold is higher, as ethane is typically the lowest priced component of NGLs sold.&#160; </font></div><div><br></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">1</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;font-size:7pt;"><a style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;" href="#s2AB1C425F68D5726B01A88D75B434628"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;">Table of Contents</font></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:7pt;"><a style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;" href="#s26AA4B5CED4051F38E975FF750EB2944"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;">Index to Financial Statements</font></a></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Producers generally elect to &#8220;reject&#8221; ethane when the price received for the ethane in the gas stream is greater than the net price received for the ethane being sold as a liquid after fractionation.&#160; </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Exploration costs</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Costs incurred in identifying areas that may warrant examination and in examining specific areas that are considered to have prospects of containing oil and natural gas reserves, including costs of drilling exploratory wells and exploratory-type stratigraphic test wells. For a complete definition of exploration costs, refer to the SEC&#8217;s Regulation&#160;S-X, Rule&#160;4-10(a)(12).</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Exploratory well</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;A well drilled to find a new field or to find a new reservoir in a field previously found to be productive of oil or natural gas in another reservoir.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Field</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;An area consisting of a single reservoir or multiple reservoirs all grouped on, or related to, the same individual geological structural feature or stratigraphic condition. The field name refers to the surface area, although it may refer to both the surface and the underground productive formations. For a complete definition of field, refer to the SEC&#8217;s Regulation&#160;S-X, Rule&#160;4-10(a)(15).</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Formation</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;A layer of rock which has distinct characteristics that differs from nearby rock.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Gross acres or gross wells</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The total acres or wells, as the case may be, in which a working interest is owned.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Held by production</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Acreage covered by a mineral lease that perpetuates a lessee&#8217;s right to operate a property as long as the property produces a minimum paying quantity of oil or natural gas.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Henry Hub price</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;A natural gas benchmark price quoted at settlement date average.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Horizontal drilling</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;A drilling technique used in certain formations where a well is drilled vertically to a certain depth and then drilled horizontally within a specified formation interval.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Infill drilling</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Drilling wells in between established producing wells to increase recovery of natural gas,&#160;oil&#160;and NGLs&#160;from a known reservoir.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">MBbl</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;One thousand barrels of crude oil, condensate or NGLs.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">MBoe</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;One thousand Boe.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Mcf</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;One thousand cubic feet of natural gas.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Mcf/d</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;One Mcf per day.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">MMBbl</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;One million barrels of crude oil, condensate or NGLs.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">MMBoe</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;One million Boe.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">MMBtu</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;One million British thermal units.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">MMcf</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;One million cubic feet of natural gas.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">MMcf/d.</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;One MMcf per day.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Net acres or net wells</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The sum of the fractional working interest owned in gross acres or gross wells, as the case may be. For example, an owner who has 50% interest in 100 acres owns 50 net acres. Likewise, an owner who has a 50% working interest in a well has a 0.50 net well.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Net production</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Production less royalties and production due to others.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Net revenue interest</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;A working interest owner&#8217;s interest in the revenues of a well after deducting proceeds allocated to royalty and overriding interests, which are owned by other parties. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">NGL(s)</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Natural gas liquid(s). Hydrocarbons found in natural gas which may be extracted as liquefied petroleum gas and natural gasoline.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">NYMEX</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The New York Mercantile Exchange.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Operator</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The individual or company responsible for the development and/or production of an oil or natural gas well or lease.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div><br></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;font-size:7pt;"><a style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;" href="#s2AB1C425F68D5726B01A88D75B434628"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;">Table of Contents</font></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:7pt;"><a style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;" href="#s26AA4B5CED4051F38E975FF750EB2944"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;">Index to Financial Statements</font></a></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Production</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">costs</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Costs incurred to operate and maintain wells and related equipment and facilities, including depreciation and applicable operating costs of support equipment and facilities and other costs of operating and maintaining those wells and related equipment and facilities. For a complete definition of production costs, refer to the SEC&#8217;s Regulation&#160;S-X, Rule&#160;4-10(a)(20).</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Productive</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">well</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;An exploratory or development well that is not a dry well and is capable of proceeds from production exceeding production expenses and taxes.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Proration unit</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;A unit that can be effectively and efficiently drained by one well, as allocated by a governmental agency having regulatory jurisdiction.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Prospect</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;A specific geographic area which, based on supporting geological, geophysical or other data and also preliminary economic analysis using reasonably anticipated prices and costs, is deemed to have potential for the discovery of commercial hydrocarbons.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Proved</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">area</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The part of a property to which proved reserves have been specifically attributed.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Proved developed reserves</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Reserves that can be expected to be recovered (i) through&#160;existing wells with existing equipment and operating methods or in which the cost of the required equipment is relatively minor compared with the cost of a new well or (ii)&#160;through installed extraction equipment and infrastructure operational at the time of the reserves estimate if the extraction is by means not involving a well.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Proved properties</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Properties with proved reserves.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Proved reserves</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Those quantities of oil, natural gas and NGLs, which, by analysis of geoscience and engineering data, can be estimated with reasonable certainty to be economically producible&#8212;from a given date forward, from known reservoirs, and under existing economic conditions, operating methods and government regulations&#8212;prior to the time at which contracts providing the right to operate expire, unless evidence indicates that renewal is reasonably certain, regardless of whether deterministic or probabilistic methods are used for the estimation. The project to extract the hydrocarbons must have commenced or the operator must be reasonably certain that it will commence the project within a reasonable time. For a complete definition of proved oil and natural gas reserves, refer to the SEC&#8217;s Regulation&#160;S-X, Rule&#160;4-10(a)(22).</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Proved undeveloped reserves</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Proved reserves that are expected to be recovered from new wells on undrilled acreage or from existing wells where a relatively major expenditure is required for recompletion. This includes infill wells, which are drilled into the same reservoir as a known producing well in order to accelerate recovery. Reserves on undrilled acreage shall be limited to those directly offsetting development spacing areas that are reasonably certain of production when drilled, unless evidence using reliable technology exists that establishes reasonable certainty of economic producibility at greater distances.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Undrilled locations can be classified as having undeveloped reserves only if a development plan has been adopted indicating that they are scheduled to be drilled within five years, unless the specific circumstances justify a longer time. Under no circumstances shall estimates for proved undeveloped reserves be attributable to any acreage for which an application of fluid injection or other improved recovery technique is contemplated, unless such techniques have been proved effective by actual projects in the same reservoir or an analogous reservoir, or by other evidence using reliable technology establishing reasonable certainty.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Realized</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">price</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The cash market price less all expected quality, transportation and demand adjustments.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Reasonable certainty</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;A high degree of confidence that quantities will be recovered. For a complete definition of reasonable certainty, refer to the SEC&#8217;s Regulation&#160;S-X, Rule&#160;4-10(a)(24).</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Recompletion</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The completion for production of an existing wellbore in another formation, or other zones within the same formation, from which the well has been previously completed.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Reliable technology</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Reliable technology is a grouping of one or more technologies (including computational methods) that has been field tested and has been demonstrated to provide reasonably certain results with consistency and repeatability in the formation being evaluated or in an analogous formation.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Reserves</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Estimated remaining quantities of oil and natural gas and related substances anticipated to be economically producible, as of a given date, by application of development projects to known accumulations. In addition, there must exist, or there must be a reasonable expectation that there will exist, the legal right to produce or a revenue interest in the production, installed means of delivering oil and natural gas or related substances to market and all permits and financing required to implement the project. Reserves should not be assigned to adjacent reservoirs isolated by major, potentially sealing, faults until those reservoirs are penetrated and evaluated as economically producible. Reserves should not be assigned to areas that are clearly separated from a known accumulation by a non-productive reservoir (i.e.,&#160;absence of reservoir, structurally low reservoir </font></div><div><br></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">3</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;font-size:7pt;"><a style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;" href="#s2AB1C425F68D5726B01A88D75B434628"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;">Table of Contents</font></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:7pt;"><a style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;" href="#s26AA4B5CED4051F38E975FF750EB2944"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;">Index to Financial Statements</font></a></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">or negative test results). Such areas may contain prospective resources (i.e.,&#160;potentially recoverable resources from undiscovered accumulations).</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Reservoir</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;A porous and permeable underground formation containing a natural accumulation of producible oil and/or natural gas that is confined by impermeable rock or water barriers and is individual and separate from other reservoirs.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Resources</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Quantities of oil and natural gas estimated to exist in naturally occurring accumulations. A portion of the resources may be estimated to be recoverable and another portion may be considered to be unrecoverable. Resources include both discovered and undiscovered accumulations.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Royalty</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;An interest in an oil and natural gas lease that gives the owner the right to receive a portion of the production from the leased acreage (or of the proceeds from the sale thereof) but does not require the owner to pay any portion of the production or development costs on the leased acreage. Royalties may be either landowner&#8217;s royalties, which are reserved by the owner of the leased acreage at the time the lease is granted, or overriding royalties, which are usually reserved by an owner of an interest in the leasehold in connection with a transfer to a subsequent owner.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Spacing</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The distance between wells producing from the same reservoir. Spacing is often expressed in terms of acres, e.g.,&#160;40-acre spacing, and is often established by regulatory agencies. For example, if wells on a 640-acre section are drilled evenly such that each well is assigned to drain 40 acres, each of the resulting 16 wells would be spaced on 40 acres per well.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Spot market price</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The cash market price for oil, natural gas or NGLs without reduction for expected quality, transportation and demand adjustments.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Spud</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Commenced drilling operations on an identified location.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Stacked hydrocarbon-bearing formations</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Vertically layered geologic zones that exist at differing underground depths and are capable of producing oil, natural gas and NGLs. The existence of stacked-hydrocarbon bearing formations enables the development of multiple hydrocarbon bearing zones from a common surface&#160;area.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Standardized</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">measure</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Discounted future net cash flows estimated by applying the average price for the last 12 months to the estimated future production of year end proved reserves. Future cash inflows are reduced by estimated future production and development costs based on period-end costs to determine pre-tax cash inflows. Future income taxes, if applicable, are computed by applying the statutory tax rate to the excess of pre-tax cash inflows over our tax basis in the oil and natural gas properties. Future net cash inflows after income taxes are discounted using a 10% annual discount rate.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Stratigraphic</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">test</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">well</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;A drilling effort, geologically directed, to obtain information pertaining to a specific geologic condition. Such wells customarily are drilled without the intent of being completed for hydrocarbon production. The classification also includes tests identified as core tests and all types of expendable holes related to hydrocarbon exploration. Stratigraphic tests are classified as &#8220;exploratory type&#8221; if not drilled in a known producing area or &#8220;development type&#8221; if drilled in a known producing area.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Undeveloped</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">acreage</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Lease acreage on which wells have not been drilled or completed to a point that would permit the production of commercial quantities of oil and natural gas regardless of whether such acreage contains proved reserves.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Unit, drilling unit or spacing unit</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The joining of all or substantially all interests in a reservoir or field, rather than a single tract, to provide for development and operation in coordination with the separate property interests. Also, the area covered by a unitization agreement.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Unproved</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">properties</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Lease acreage with no proved reserves.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Wellbore</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The hole drilled by the bit that is equipped for oil, natural gas and NGLs production on a completed well. Also called well or borehole.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Working</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">interest</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The right granted to the lessee of a property to develop and produce and own oil, natural gas or other minerals. The working interest owners bear the exploration, development and operating costs on either a cash, penalty or carried basis.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Workover</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Operations on a producing well to restore or increase production.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">WTI</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;West Texas Intermediate. A market index price for oil of certain specifications that is widely quoted by financial markets.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Zipper Fracs</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Hydraulically fracturing adjacent wells in parallel, with one or more wells holding frac pressure while the adjacent well is fractured.</font></div><div><br></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">4</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><a name="s2E4079102A1D5A2A887C3BC82D65A388"></a></div><div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;font-size:7pt;"><a style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;" href="#s2AB1C425F68D5726B01A88D75B434628"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;">Table of Contents</font></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:7pt;"><a style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;" href="#s26AA4B5CED4051F38E975FF750EB2944"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;">Index to Financial Statements</font></a></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:10px;text-align:center;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">CAUTIONARY STATEMENT REGARDING FORWARD-LOOKING STATEMENTS</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The information in this Form 10-K includes &#8220;forward-looking statements.&#8221; style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:32px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div Our development drilling plan is comprised exclusively of horizontal drilling with an ongoing focus to increase capital efficiency by reducing drilling and completion cycle times, optimizing completions and reducing costs. We expect that further optimization in the field, which will include drilling long and extra-long laterals, pad drilling, shared facilities and zipper fracs will continue to improve our well economics.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:32px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">We divide our current area of operation within the southern Delaware Basin into three distinct project areas: Cochise, Whiskey River and Big Tex. The Cochise project area lies in the northern part of our acreage position and straddles Ward and Winkler Counties. Whiskey River is in the central part of our overall leasehold position and primarily lies just west of the junction between Ward, Reeves and Pecos Counties in Texas. The Big Tex project area is our southernmost leasehold position and lies in northern Pecos County. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:32px;font-size:10pt;"><font During this same period, our average daily production grew from </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">9,785</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#160;Boe/d in the first quarter of </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2017</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;to </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">38,413</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;Boe/d in the fourth quarter of </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">. During </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, we began production on </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">59</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;gross (</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">48.0</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;net) wells, of which we operated </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">45</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;gross (</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">42.4</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;net) wells. While we have producing wells in these distinct targets, the formations primarily targeted have been the Lower and Upper Wolfcamp A and the 3</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt">rd</sup></font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;Bone Spring. Of the </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">45</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;gross operated wells that we began producing from during </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">36</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;were in the Lower Wolfcamp A and </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">five</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;were in the 3</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt">rd</sup></font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;Bone Spring. Other operators continue to maintain active drilling and completion operations on acreage offsetting our acreage position. We monitor this offset activity, especially with respect to downspacing pilots, and will adjust our future development plans to allow for the optimal development of our acreage position. We also believe potential development opportunities exist on portions of our acreage in the Brushy Canyon, Avalon Shale, 1</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt">st</sup></font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;Bone Spring and Pennsylvanian aged formations.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Our contiguous acreage position enables the drilling of long laterals, resulting in significant drilling efficiencies that enhance the economic development of our acreage position. Of our approximately </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">1,800</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;gross horizontal drilling locations as of </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">86%</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;are classified as long or extra-long. We consider laterals of </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">5,640</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;feet and lower as standard length, laterals between </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">5,640</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;feet and </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">8,000</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;feet to be long, and laterals greater than </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">8,000</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;feet to be extra-long. The ability to drill long-lateral wells improves our returns by (i)&#160;increasing our EUR per well, (ii)&#160;allowing us to contact more reservoir rock with fewer vertical wellbores (thus reducing drilling and completion costs on a per unit basis) and (iii)&#160;allowing us to hold by production more acreage per horizontal well drilled. Additionally, the contiguous nature of our acreage provides economies of scale by allowing us to better share our infrastructure among wells across our acreage position.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">In conjunction with developing our acreage for optimized production of our oil and natural gas reserves, we have also developed our own water system, which enables us to source, store and dispose of water efficiently. As of </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, we had approximately </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">5,100</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;net surface acres, which allows us the operational and financial control to source, dispose, store and transport water. Our water infrastructure includes approximately (i) </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">9.3</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;MMBbl of water storage capacity, (ii) </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">30</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;miles of fresh water pipelines and </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">130</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;miles of produced water pipelines, which allows us to largely eliminate water trucking in all phases of our operation, (iii)&#160;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">150</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;MBbl/d of water sourcing capacity and (iv)&#160;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">200</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;MBbl/d of water disposal capacity. Accordingly, we have available disposal capacity and sufficient sources of fresh water to support our current development program. Surplus fresh water and disposal capacity generated approximately </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">$0.8 million</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;of other operating revenues in </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, and opportunities to leverage surplus capacities will be evaluated in 2019.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div><a name="s2ADF35C63F955E3089C33D07E7C97A9E"></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Proved Reserves</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:32px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Internal Controls Over Reserve Estimating Process.</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Our proved reserve estimates as of </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2017</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2016</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, were prepared by Ryder Scott Company, LP (&#8220;Ryder Scott&#8221;), our third party, independent engineering firm. Within Ryder Scott, the technical person primarily responsible for preparing the estimates set forth in the Ryder Scott reserves report incorporated herein is Mr. Stephen E. Gardner. Mr. Gardner, a Licensed Professional Engineer in the States of Colorado and Texas, has been practicing consulting petroleum engineering at Ryder Scott since 2006 and has more than 13 years of practical experience in the estimation and evaluation of petroleum reserves. He graduated from Brigham Young University in 2001 (summa cum laude) with a Bachelor of Science Degree in Mechanical Engineering. Mr. Gardner meets or exceeds the education, training and experience requirements set forth in the Standards Pertaining to the Estimating and Auditing of Oil and Gas Reserves Information promulgated by the Society of Petroleum Engineers; and is proficient in judiciously applying industry standard practices to evaluations as well as applying Securities and Exchange Commission (&#8220;SEC&#8221;) and other industry reserves definitions and guidelines. Ryder Scott does not own an interest in any of our properties, and is not employed by us on a contingent basis. A copy of Ryder Scott&#8217;s proved reserve report as of </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;is included as an exhibit to this Form 10-K.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:32px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:32px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The preparation of our proved reserve estimates was completed in accordance with our internal control procedures. These procedures are intended to ensure reliability of reserve estimations. The Company&#8217;s internal controls over reserve estimates include reconciliation and review controls, including an internal review of assumptions used in the estimation as well as ultimate approval of our capital budget and review of our development plan by our senior management. The development plan underlying the Company&#8217;s proved undeveloped reserves (&#8220;PUDs&#8221;) is further subject to internal controls, including (i) a comparison of future development costs to our historical expenditures, our future development plan, and financial capabilities and (ii) an evaluation of the estimated profitability of each location at the time the report is prepared. The development plan underlying the Company&#8217;s PUDs, adopted every year by senior management, is based on the best information available at the time of adoption. As factors such as commodity price, service costs, performance data and asset mix are subject to change, the Company occasionally revises its development plan. Development plan revisions include deferrals, removals and substitutions of previously scheduled </font></div><div><br></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">8</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;font-size:7pt;"><a style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;" href="#s2AB1C425F68D5726B01A88D75B434628"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;">Table of Contents</font></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:7pt;"><a style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;" href="#s26AA4B5CED4051F38E975FF750EB2944"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:7pt;font-style:italic;">Index to Financial Statements</font></a></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">PUD reserve locations. These occasional changes achieve the purpose of maximizing profitability and are in the best interest of the Company&#8217;s shareholders.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:32px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Our internal professional staff worked closely with our independent reserve engineers to ensure the integrity, accuracy and timeliness of the data used to calculate our proved reserves. Our internal technical team members met with our independent reserve engineers periodically during the period covered by the proved reserve report to discuss the assumptions and methods used in the proved reserve estimation process. We provide historical information to Ryder Scott for our properties, such as ownership interest, oil and natural gas production, realized commodity prices and operating and development costs. Our Planning and Reserves Manager is primarily responsible for overseeing the preparation of the Company&#8217;s reserve estimates. Our Planning and Reserves Manager is a reservoir engineer with more than 17 years of reservoir and operations experience and has been licensed by the Texas Board of Professional Engineers since 2005.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:32px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:32px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Estimation of Proved Reserves.</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The estimates of proved reserves as of </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;are based upon the use of technical and economic data including, but not limited to, well logs, geologic maps, seismic data, production data, historical price and cost information and property ownership interests. The reserves were estimated using deterministic and analogy methods; these estimates were prepared in accordance with generally accepted petroleum engineering and evaluation principles. Standard engineering and geoscience methods, such as reservoir modeling, performance analysis, volumetric analysis and analogy, which were considered to be appropriate and necessary to establish reserve quantities and reserve categorization that conform to SEC definitions and rules and regulations, were also used. As in all aspects of oil and natural gas evaluation, there are uncertainties inherent in the interpretation of engineering and geoscience data; therefore, these estimates necessarily represent only informed professional judgment.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:32px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Summary of Reserves.</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The following table sets forth the Company&#8217;s estimated net proved reserves as of </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2017</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2016</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, based on the proved reserve report as of such dates by Ryder Scott, prepared in accordance with the rules and regulations of the SEC. During </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, we began production on </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">59</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;gross (</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">48.0</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;net) wells. This activity resulted in a combined increase of </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">35.7</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;MMBoe due to infill reserves from a proved field. Over this time period, we also had approximately </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">12.7</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#160;MMBoe of </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">upward</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;revisions to prior estimates, due primarily to </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">11.2</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;MMBoe of positive performance revisions.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:32px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Proved Undeveloped Reserves</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">PUDs include those reserves that are expected to be recovered from new wells on undrilled acreage or from existing wells where a relatively major expenditure is required for recompletion. Undrilled locations may be classified as proved reserves on acreage directly offsetting developed wells if the PUD locations are reasonably certain of production when drilled or where reliable technology provides reasonable certainty of economic producibility. Undrilled locations may be classified as having PUDs only if a development plan has been adopted indicating that they are scheduled to be drilled within five years, unless specific circumstances justify a longer time. As of </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, all </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">60</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;of our PUD drilling locations are scheduled to be developed within five years of their initial booking. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">For PUD locations that are more than one development spacing area from developed producing locations, we utilized reliable geologic and engineering technology when booking PUDs. We incorporated public and proprietary data from multiple sources to establish geologic continuity of each formation and their producing properties. This included seismic data and interpretations (3-D and micro seismic), open hole log information (collected both vertically and horizontally) and petrophysical analysis of that log data, mud logs, gas sample analyses, measurements of total organic content, thermal maturity, test production, fluid properties, core data and significant statistical performance data yielding predictable and repeatable reserve estimates within certain analogous areas. These locations were limited to only those areas where both established geologic consistency and sufficient statistical performance data could be demonstrated to provide reasonably certain results. In all other areas, we restricted proved undeveloped locations to development spacing areas that are immediately adjacent to developed spacing areas.</font></div><div We expect to be able to meet this commitment that will be sourced from our properties in the southern Delaware Basin.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">We sell substantially all of our natural gas from our Cochise acreage under a long-term gathering and processing agreement entered into in September 2015, and substantially all of our natural gas from our Whiskey River acreage under a long-term gathering and processing agreement entered into in October 2016. We sell substantially all of our natural gas from our Big Tex acreage pursuant to a short-term gathering and processing agreement expiring in the fall of 2019. Substantially all of our natural gas production is transported from the wellhead by third-party gathering lines to natural gas processing facilities. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">Major Customers</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">We sell our oil, natural gas and NGL production to purchasers at market prices. We sell our production to a relatively small number of customers, as is customary in our business. For </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, revenues from Trafigura Trading,&#160;LLC accounted for approximately </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">85%</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;of our total revenue and no other purchaser accounted for 10% or more of our revenue. The loss of this purchaser could materially and adversely affect our revenues in the short-term. However, based on the current demand for oil, natural gas and NGLs, and the availability of other purchasers, we believe that the loss of any of our purchasers would not have a long-term material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations because oil, natural gas and NGLs are fungible products with well-established markets.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">Infrastructure</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Our infrastructure strategy includes owning sufficient tracts of surface acreage to (i)&#160;allow us to control water supply for drilling and completions, (ii)&#160;provide ease of pipeline installation, (iii)&#160;allow construction of storage for both fresh and treated produced water and (iv)&#160;allow us to control facilities for disposal of flowback and produced water. In addition, we have supplemental agreements that provide for fresh water sourcing and produced water storage and disposal from surface acreage owned by adjacent landowners as needed. As of </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, we owned approximately </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">5,100</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;net surface acres. Our water infrastructure consists of approximately (i) </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">9.3</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;MMBbl of water storage capacity, (ii) </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">30</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;miles of fresh water pipelines, (iii) </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">130</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;miles of produced water pipelines, (iv)&#160;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">150</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;MBbl/d of water sourcing capacity and (v)&#160;</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">200</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;MBbl/d of water disposal capacity. Our infrastructure allows us to largely eliminate water trucking in all phases of our operations. Accordingly, we have available disposal capacity and sufficient sources of fresh water to support our current and anticipated development program. Surplus fresh water and surplus disposal capacity generated approximately </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">$0.8 million</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">&#32;revenue in </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, and opportunities to leverage surplus capacities will be evaluated in 2019. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">Competition</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:30px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The oil and natural gas industry is intensely competitive, and we compete with other companies that have greater resources. Many of these companies not only explore for and produce oil and natural gas, but also carry on midstream and refining operations and market petroleum and other products on a regional, national or worldwide basis.
